newsitem.title: USA: Pena says hopes to avoid U.S. reserve oil sale.
newsitem.headline: Pena says hopes to avoid U.S. reserve oil sale.

text.p: U.S. Energy Secretary Federico Pena said Tuesday he did not know whether the Clinton administration's proposed sale of government reserve oil would be in the balanced-budget deal, and said he would try to prevent the sale.
Under questioning by the Senate Energy Committee, Pena said it was uncertain whether the $1.145 billion oil sale from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve for 2002 would be in the five-year budget deal.
Later he told Reuters that the White House-congressional discussions on the balanced budget plan had not yet reached that level of detail.
Since the White House's proposed budget had a plan to sell SPR oil in 2002 to help defray the deficit, Energy Department officials said they assumed it was still a working proposal.
But Pena reiterated to the Senate panel that he considered the SPR sale proposal to be a "placemarker" in the White House budget plan.
"It is my view that we ought not to sell any more oil" from the reserve, he said, adding that he was working with the administration to find alternatives to the sale.

"Based on recent Energy Information Administration import estimates, the days of import protection from the SPR will decrease to 46 days in 2002, implying a significantly increased dependence on private stocks, over which the Federal Government has virtually no control, to meet our international obligations," Pena said in prepared remarks for the hearing.

The International Energy Agency, an organization of oil importing countries including the United States, in testimony committee also said it was concerned that U.S. oil imports were rising while government-held reserve have slipped.

Committee Chairman Frank Murkowski said the three SPR sales in the last 18 months had cost taxpayers close to $500 million because the oil was bought years ago at high market prices, and sold at sharply lower prices.
The hearing was on several bills related to the SPR, including Murkowski's bill to reauthorize the SPR's overseeing law for five years.

The Alaska Republican said the current year-to-year reauthorization could lead to risky lapses of the law as Congress waits until late in the year to move on the bill and there often are efforts to attach unrelated items to it.

But Pena said he backed a one-year reauthorization because the department intends later this year to offer legislation to change SPR provisions "so that they more adequately reflect the operation of the program as it exists today and the Administration's policies on the use and size of the reserve."

Pena also said he backed a measure that would give the department authority to lease unused space to store foreign-owned oil. But he said a bill sponsored by Hawaii Democratic Sen. Daniel Akaka to require that lease proceeds be used to buy more oil for the SPR could raise "budgetary problems."
